intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, when crowds are thinner and the light is magical. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver based near Siem Reap's Old Market area to navigate the vast complex efficiently. Given a late Day 1 arrival, begin this on Day 2 morning fully rested. Stay in a guesthouse within 2km of the Angkor gate to minimize transit time.

experiences.name: Bayon Temple & Ta Prohm Ruins
experiences.description: Visit the enigmatic Bayon with its 216 stone faces and the jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm (Tomb Raider temple) on the same day as Angkor Wat using a 3-day pass. Staying near Pub Street or the Old Market in Siem Reap puts you within a short tuk-tuk ride, making afternoon visits practical even after a late start.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry from Sihanoukville to the tranquil Saracen Bay on Koh Rong Samloem for crystal-clear waters and white sand. Book accommodation directly on the island to avoid costly and time-consuming daily ferry trips. Ideal for Days 5–7, allowing full beach days without wasted travel. Snorkeling gear rental is available on the island.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace & Silver Pagoda
experiences.description: Discover Cambodia's royal heritage at the stunning Royal Palace complex, home to the Silver Pagoda with its emerald Buddha. Stay in the BKK1 or Riverside district of Phnom Penh to be within walking distance or a short tuk-tuk ride. Schedule this for Day 3 or 4 after Siem Reap, arriving by bus in the morning to maximize your afternoon visit.

experiences.name: Khmer Street Food Tour at Phsar Thmei (Central Market)
experiences.description: Join a guided evening street food walk around Phnom Penh's Central Market and surrounding streets, sampling amok fish curry, lok lak beef, and fresh sugarcane juice. Evening tours avoid the midday heat and are more vibrant with local vendors. Staying in the BKK1 or Daun Penh district keeps you close to the market, making this a spontaneous and budget-friendly experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Siem Reap Boutique Stay, freshen up, then take a leisurely walk along Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area to get oriented. Browse local handicrafts and soak in the atmosphere without spending much.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Night Market on Sivatha Boulevard — free to browse. Enjoy the lively street atmosphere and pick up a cheap souvenir if desired.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or at a local noodle stall (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Old Market — affordable local Khmer dishes like Amok and Lok Lak (~$4–6 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a local money changer for better rates. USD is widely accepted in Cambodia. Tuk-tuks from the airport cost roughly $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Early sunrise visit to Angkor Wat (purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass for ~$62 USD — best value). Arrive before 5:30 AM to witness the iconic sunrise reflection over the temple. Explore the outer galleries and bas-reliefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex — visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon, Elephant Terrace, and Terrace of the Leper King. Take a packed lunch to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap by tuk-tuk. Visit the Angkor Night Market for local street food and cultural performances. Browse free art galleries nearby.

meals.breakfast: Baguette and coffee from a street vendor near the hotel (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local bakery or market stall near Angkor (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Soup Dragon Restaurant — affordable Khmer and Asian fusion near Old Market (~$4–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the full day (~$12–15 USD) — they wait while you explore. Bring water, sunscreen, and a hat. November weather is dry season and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 2 of the Angkor Pass to visit Ta Prohm — the jungle temple famously featured in Tomb Raider, with massive tree roots engulfing the ruins. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Banteay Kdei and the serene Sra Srang reservoir. Then head to Banteay Srei (~30 km from Siem Reap) — a smaller but exquisitely carved 10th-century temple in pink sandstone, often called the 'Jewel of Khmer Art.'
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, visit the free Artisans Angkor workshop to watch local craftspeople carve silk and stone. Then relax at a riverside café along the Siem Reap River.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local rice porridge (Bobor) from a street stall (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Banteay Srei village (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Marum Restaurant — social enterprise training restaurant, affordable and delicious Khmer food (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires extra travel — negotiate with your tuk-tuk driver for a combined day rate (~$18–20 USD). Dress modestly for temple visits (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 3 of the Angkor Pass. Visit the less-crowded but impressive Preah Khan temple — a large flat complex with long corridors, ancient trees, and peaceful atmosphere. Then see Neak Pean and Ta Som.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Pre Rup and East Mebon temples. Climb Pre Rup for panoramic views over the Cambodian plains — excellent in the late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost Apsara dance performance at a local restaurant (many offer free shows with dinner). Try the Apsara Theatre for an authentic cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: French baguette with eggs from a street café (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup from a roadside stall near the temples (~$2 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner with Apsara dance show at a local restaurant (~$6–8 USD including show)

day_by_day.notes: This is your last day using the 3-day Angkor Pass — make the most of it. The northern temple circuit is less visited and more peaceful than the main circuit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Cambodian Cultural Village (~$15 USD entry) — a living museum showcasing all of Cambodia's ethnic groups, traditional houses, and cultural performances. Great for history and culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free War Museum Cambodia — an outdoor collection of tanks, artillery, landmines, and weapons from Cambodia's turbulent 20th-century history. Sobering and educational.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pub Street area for happy hour drinks (~$0.50 draft beers). Visit the Angkor Night Market for local crafts, clothing, and street food. Watch free traditional music performances.

meals.breakfast: Khmer breakfast — sticky rice with mango from a market stall (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Buffet lunch at Cambodian Cultural Village (included or ~$3–4 USD add-on)
meals.dinner: Street food tour along Pub Street — try grilled meats, spring rolls, and noodles (~$3–4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The War Museum is free but donations are encouraged. November is peak season so book transport in advance. Today is a good rest day from temple trekking.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or shared minivan from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (~5–6 hours, ~$6–8 USD via Giant Ibis or Mekong Express). Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check in to a budget guesthouse (~$8–15 USD/night). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (~$10 USD entry) — stunning Khmer architecture and the famous Emerald Buddha.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay riverfront promenade — free and scenic. Watch the sunset over the Tonle Sap and Mekong river confluence.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before departing Siem Reap — banh mi sandwich (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus or stop at a roadside restaurant (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — social enterprise with affordable Khmer tapas and fusion dishes (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket a day in advance. Giant Ibis is the most reliable budget bus company. Store luggage at the bus station or guesthouse while exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically important site documenting the Khmer Rouge atrocities (~$5 USD entry). Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Killing Fields of Choeung Ek (~$3 USD entry + $3 tuk-tuk) — an essential historical site with an excellent audio guide included. Spend time reflecting at the memorial stupa.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a beautiful Art Deco building with local goods, jewelry, and food. Browse freely and pick up affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Khmer porridge (Bobor) at a local café near the guesthouse (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Tuol Sleng — rice and curry (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant — social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine in a lovely garden setting (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: These sites are emotionally heavy — take breaks as needed. Dress respectfully. The audio guide at Choeung Ek is included in the entry fee and highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (~4 hours, ~$6–8 USD). Sihanoukville is the gateway to Cambodia's beaches and islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Sihanoukville and take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island (~$25 USD round-trip ferry). Check in to a budget beach bungalow (~$15–20 USD/night). Relax on the stunning Saracen Bay beach.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach — free and spectacular. Enjoy bioluminescent plankton in the water after dark (best experienced by swimming or kayaking at night).

meals.breakfast: Grab food before departing Phnom Penh — local market stall (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Snack on ferry or at Sihanoukville port (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Beach bungalow restaurant or local shack on Koh Rong Samloem — fresh grilled fish (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during peak season (November is busy). Koh Rong Samloem is quieter and more pristine than Koh Rong. Bring cash as ATMs are limited on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day on Koh Rong Samloem. Explore the island on foot — hike to the secluded Lazy Beach on the other side of the island (~45-minute jungle trail, free). Swim in crystal-clear turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak (~$5–8 USD/half day) and paddle around the coastline, exploring hidden coves and coral reefs. Snorkeling gear rental available (~$3–5 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Bonfire on the beach (organized by many guesthouses — free or minimal cost). Stargaze from the beach — minimal light pollution makes for an incredible night sky.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit platter and coffee at the bungalow restaurant (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from the guesthouse or eat at Lazy Beach's small café (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Barbecue seafood platter on the beach — shared with fellow travelers (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral reefs. The jungle trail to Lazy Beach can be muddy — wear proper shoes. No motorized vehicles on most of the island — it's very peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise swim. Pack up and take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville. Browse the local market in Sihanoukville for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a bus or shared taxi back toward Phnom Penh for international connections, or explore Otres Beach near Sihanoukville (~$3 tuk-tuk) — a quieter, less developed beach for a final relaxing afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Sihanoukville or Phnom Penh depending on departure plans. Reflect on 10 incredible days of Cambodian history, culture, and beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final beach breakfast — eggs, toast, and fresh juice (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Seafood noodles at Sihanoukville port market (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell Khmer feast — Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and fresh coconut at a local restaurant (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm onward transport and flight details. Keep small USD bills for tips and final purchases. Total estimated budget for 10 days (excluding flights): $250–350 USD including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and freshen up after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Siem Reap Boutique Stay, then take a leisurely stroll along the Siem Reap River Walk and explore the Old French Quarter architecture. Visit Psar Chaa (Old Market) to get oriented with local goods, spices, and handicrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street area for a relaxed evening. Explore the vibrant night market stalls and soak in the lively atmosphere of central Siem Reap.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or light snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a casual bite at a riverside café near the Old Market — try a Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) for around $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant or Cuisine Wat Damnak area — enjoy authentic Khmer set meals for $8–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to Cambodian Riel at the airport or a local exchange booth. USD is widely accepted in Siem Reap. November is the start of the dry season — expect pleasant weather around 25–30°C.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a sunrise visit to Angkor Wat — one of the world's greatest archaeological wonders. Arrive by 5:30 AM to witness the iconic reflection in the moat. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex: visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Elephant Terrace. Take a shaded break and hydrate — the complex is large.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for a rest, then visit the Angkor Night Market for souvenirs, silk scarves, and local crafts. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack from a street vendor near Angkor Wat gate — sticky rice or banana pancake ($1–2)
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the open-air restaurants just outside the Angkor complex — Khmer curry with rice for $5–8
meals.dinner: Dinner with Apsara dance show at Angkor Village Restaurant or Temple Balcony — $15–25 per person including performance

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) — it offers the best value if you plan to visit over multiple days. Wear light breathable clothing, sunscreen, and a hat. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ta Prohm temple — the famous 'Tomb Raider' temple where giant silk-cotton tree roots dramatically engulf ancient stone ruins. Walk through moss-covered corridors and hidden chambers for a truly atmospheric experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — located about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. Known for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, it is considered one of the finest examples of Khmer art. Hire a tuk-tuk for the round trip.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel, then dine in the Kandal Village neighborhood — a quieter, boutique area of Siem Reap with art galleries, independent cafés, and creative restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — Khmer-style eggs, baguette, and iced coffee ($3–5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop near Banteay Srei — local rice dishes ($3–6)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or The Sugar Palm in Kandal Village — refined Khmer cuisine for $12–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hire a knowledgeable tuk-tuk driver for the day (around $15–20 USD) who can navigate both Ta Prohm and Banteay Srei efficiently. Respect temple dress codes — shoulders and knees must be covered.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for deep historical context on the Khmer Empire. The museum houses over 1,000 artifacts including sculptures, ceramics, and inscriptions. A great complement to temple visits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Preah Khan temple — a sprawling, partially restored complex with long atmospheric corridors, Buddhist shrines, and a serene jungle feel. Less crowded than Angkor Wat and equally impressive.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a shadow puppet (Sbek Thom) performance or visit a local artisan workshop to learn about traditional Cambodian crafts. Walk through the Night Market and try street food snacks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel or Café Central near the museum — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee ($4–6)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Preah Khan — amok (fish curry in coconut) with rice for $5–8
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Night Market — grilled skewers, spring rolls, fresh coconut, and mango sticky rice for $5–10

day_by_day.notes: The Angkor National Museum entry is $12 USD. Audio guides are available and highly recommended. November evenings are comfortable — ideal for outdoor night market browsing.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Phnom Kulen National Park (about 50 km from Siem Reap) — a sacred mountain plateau considered the birthplace of the Khmer Empire. Hike to the River of a Thousand Lingas, carved directly into the riverbed, and visit the reclining Buddha carved from a single boulder.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim in the natural waterfall pools at Phnom Kulen — a refreshing break surrounded by jungle. Explore the forest trails and smaller shrines on the plateau.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Enjoy a relaxing traditional Khmer massage to recover from the day's hiking ($10–15 for one hour at a reputable spa).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before early departure — Khmer porridge (Bobor) or toast with eggs
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from local vendors at the park entrance — grilled corn, rice parcels, and fresh fruit ($3–5)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant or Haven Restaurant (a social enterprise training vulnerable youth) — $10–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Entry to Phnom Kulen is $20 USD per person. Hire a driver for the day ($25–35). The road can be rough — start early to avoid afternoon crowds. Wear sturdy shoes for hiking.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh by bus or minivan (approximately 6 hours, $8–12 USD) or by domestic flight (35 min, ~$60–80 USD). Enjoy the countryside scenery en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check in to a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel near the riverfront. Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the stunning official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring golden spires and a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Tonle Sap and Mekong riverfront promenade (Sisowath Quay). Watch the sunset over the confluence of the rivers and enjoy the lively waterfront atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before departure from Siem Reap
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a roadside stop — local rice dishes or sandwiches ($3–5)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant (social enterprise, traditional Khmer cuisine) or Friends Restaurant on the riverfront — $10–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your Siem Reap to Phnom Penh transport in advance. The bus is comfortable and scenic. Royal Palace entry is $10 USD — dress modestly. Phnom Penh is more urban and fast-paced than Siem Reap.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply sobering but essential historical site documenting the Khmer Rouge atrocities. Take time to absorb the exhibits and personal stories. Audio guides available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial, located 15 km outside the city. The memorial stupa houses thousands of skulls and the site offers a moving and important reflection on Cambodia's tragic recent history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center. Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) with its distinctive Art Deco dome for evening shopping. Decompress with dinner in a calmer setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a riverfront café — French-style baguette with pâté (a colonial legacy), iced coffee ($3–5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Tuol Sleng — soup or sandwiches at a local café ($4–7)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Phnom Penh or a riverside restaurant — Khmer BBQ or lok lak (stir-fried beef) for $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Both Tuol Sleng ($8 USD) and Choeung Ek ($6 USD) are emotionally heavy sites. Allow yourself time and space to process. Hire a tuk-tuk for the day (~$15–20) to travel between sites comfortably.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville by bus (approximately 4 hours, $6–10 USD), then take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island (45–60 min, $15–20 USD round trip) — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and tranquil islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay on Koh Rong Samloem. Check in to a mid-range beach bungalow. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the pristine white sand beach, swimming in turquoise waters, and snorkeling over coral reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach. After dark, look for bioluminescent plankton glowing in the shallow water — a magical natural phenomenon common on this island.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel in Phnom Penh before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch on arrival at the island — fresh seafood grilled on the beach, coconut rice, and tropical fruit ($6–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront bungalow restaurant — whole grilled fish, prawn curry, or Khmer noodles ($8–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during peak season. Bring cash — ATMs are limited on the island. Pack reef-safe sunscreen and insect repellent. November is dry season — excellent beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise walk along the deserted beach. Join a guided snorkeling trip around the island's coral reefs to spot colorful fish, sea turtles, and vibrant marine life ($15–25 per person including gear).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike through the jungle interior of Koh Rong Samloem to the viewpoint for panoramic ocean views. Alternatively, kayak along the coastline and explore hidden coves and mangrove channels.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on the island — enjoy a bonfire or beach barbecue. Stargaze from the beach (minimal light pollution) and enjoy the peaceful island atmosphere before heading back to the mainland tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at bungalow — fresh fruit platter, eggs, and coffee ($3–5)
meals.lunch: Beach shack lunch — grilled squid, papaya salad, and fresh coconut water ($6–9)
meals.dinner: Farewell island dinner at a beachfront restaurant — seafood platter or Cambodian fish amok with rice and a local Angkor beer ($10–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Respect the island's fragile ecosystem — take all rubbish with you, avoid touching coral, and use reef-safe products. The island has limited electricity (often solar-powered) — charge devices when possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville (departs around 8:00–9:00 AM). Travel back to Phnom Penh by bus or shared taxi. Alternatively, fly directly from Sihanoukville to your departure city if applicable.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before departure, revisit a favorite spot in Phnom Penh — browse the Russian Market (Phsar Tuol Tom Poung) for last-minute souvenirs, silk, gems, and handicrafts at good prices.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Cambodia. Reflect on the journey over a memorable meal. Head to the airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the island before the ferry — banana pancake and coffee ($2–4)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Phnom Penh — revisit a favorite restaurant or try Cambodian BBQ for a final feast ($8–15)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Phnom Penh — panoramic city views with Khmer cuisine or fusion food ($12–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Keep some USD and Riel for last-minute tips, transport, and airport snacks. Cambodia's departure tax is typically included in your ticket. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged to Siem Reap Boutique Stay with a welcome cold towel and refreshments in the vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique hotel, freshen up, and enjoy a leisurely orientation walk through the charming French Quarter of Siem Reap. Visit the Old Market (Psar Chas) area for a gentle introduction to local crafts, silks, and artisan goods without the pressure of a full tour.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel rooftop or a nearby riverside terrace bar. Stroll along Pub Street area for atmosphere, then enjoy a welcome dinner at a premier Khmer fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and fruit platter upon hotel arrival, or a quick stop at a stylish café such as Marum or Miss Wong for a light bite
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — a celebrated tasting-menu restaurant showcasing refined Khmer cuisine using seasonal Cambodian ingredients; reserve in advance

day_by_day.notes: Request an early check-in with the hotel in advance. November is the tail end of the wet season transitioning into the dry, cool season — expect pleasant temperatures around 26–30°C with minimal rain. Pack light layers for air-conditioned venues.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise tour of Angkor Wat — the world's largest religious monument. Arrive before dawn (around 5:15 AM) with a private guide and photographer to capture the iconic reflection in the moat. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers in the golden morning light before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue within the Angkor Archaeological Park to Angkor Thom — the last great capital of the Khmer Empire. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by the hotel served in a shaded pavilion within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a traditional Khmer herbal bath and 90-minute massage at the hotel spa. Evening at leisure with a private dinner reservation.

meals.breakfast: Pre-departure light breakfast box prepared by the hotel (fruit, pastries, coffee) taken before the 5 AM departure
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic in Angkor Park — chilled prawns, Cambodian rice salads, fresh tropical fruit, and iced beverages arranged by the hotel concierge
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sugar Palm Restaurant — elegant Cambodian home-style cooking in a refined setting; try the fish amok and lok lak beef

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass in advance through your guide or hotel concierge. Wear light, breathable clothing and a hat; bring sunscreen and a refillable water bottle. Temples require covered shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle-clad temples of Ta Prohm — famously left entwined with massive silk-cotton and strangler fig trees, creating a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere. Follow with a visit to Preah Khan, a vast temple complex dedicated to the father of Jayavarman VII, known for its long columned corridors and peaceful atmosphere away from main tourist traffic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the lesser-known but stunning Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — located about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. Renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in all of Angkor. En route, stop at the Landmine Museum to learn about Cambodia's painful history and ongoing demining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an exclusive private Apsara dance performance — classical Khmer court dance listed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage — arranged at a traditional sala with a set dinner included.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel — choose from a Khmer breakfast spread (rice porridge with ginger and fish) or Western options with fresh tropical juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a curated local restaurant near Banteay Srei — try Sala Kdei for fresh Cambodian dishes in a garden setting
meals.dinner: Set dinner accompanying the private Apsara performance — traditional Khmer multi-course feast including amok, grilled fish with kroeung paste, and palm sugar desserts

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is best visited in the morning or late afternoon for optimal light for photography. Hire an air-conditioned private vehicle for the day given the distances involved.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap — an immersive, world-class museum chronicling the Khmer Empire through galleries of sculpture, artifacts, and multimedia presentations. The Gallery of 1000 Buddhas is particularly striking. Afterward, explore the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique, where you can watch skilled craftspeople restore traditional Khmer arts including stone carving, silk weaving, and lacquerware.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cooking class experience with a celebrated local chef — visit a morning market together to select ingredients, then prepare three to four traditional Khmer dishes including fish amok, green mango salad, and Khmer red curry. Classes typically held in beautiful garden settings.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise on Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Cruise past floating villages and observe local fishing communities as the sun dips below the horizon. Champagne and canapés served on board.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — fresh baguettes, Cambodian omelets, local fruits including dragon fruit and rambutan
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as your lunch — a truly immersive culinary experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — one of Cambodia's most prestigious restaurants, helmed by celebrated chef Luu Meng; sophisticated Khmer cuisine in an elegant open-air setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and sunset cruise through your hotel concierge at least 48 hours in advance. The Tonlé Sap is at its fullest in November post-rainy season, offering spectacular views of the expanded lake.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Beng Mealea — a spectacular 12th-century temple located about 68 km east of Siem Reap, largely unrestored and consumed by jungle. Far fewer visitors than Angkor, creating an adventurous, Indiana Jones-like atmosphere. Explore crumbling galleries, massive stone blocks, and hidden courtyards with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Koh Ker — an ancient remote temple complex that served briefly as the Khmer Empire's capital in the 10th century. The pyramid-shaped Prasat Thom rising 36 meters above the jungle canopy is the centerpiece. Combine both temples into a full-day archaeological adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap (approximately 2-hour drive). Relax at the hotel with a private in-room dinner or spa treatment. Alternatively, explore the Night Market and Angkor Night Market for premium silk scarves, handmade jewelry, and artisan souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — egg dishes, fresh fruit, strong Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box from the hotel enjoyed at Beng Mealea — sandwiches, local snacks, fresh fruit, and cold drinks
meals.dinner: In-room private dining experience or dinner at Embassy Restaurant — contemporary Cambodian cuisine with an extensive wine list in a colonial-style villa

day_by_day.notes: Beng Mealea and Koh Ker require a separate entry fee from the Angkor Pass. The roads are paved but the journey is long — depart by 7:00 AM. Wear sturdy shoes for uneven temple terrain. Bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Private flight or premium road transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 1 hour by air or 6 hours by road — air recommended for luxury travel). Upon arrival, check in to a luxury hotel such as Raffles Hotel Le Royal or Rosewood Phnom Penh. Begin exploration with a visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring stunning Khmer architecture and the famous Emerald Buddha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — a beautiful terracotta pavilion housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts spanning the pre-Angkorian to post-Angkorian periods. Afterward, stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverfront promenade where the Mekong, Tonlé Sap, and Bassac rivers converge.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the sky bar of the Rosewood Phnom Penh or Top of the World bar at Vattanac Capital Tower with panoramic city views. Dinner at a premier restaurant in the capital.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Siem Reap hotel before transfer
meals.lunch: Lunch at Khéma La Poste — a refined French-Cambodian brasserie set inside Phnom Penh's beautifully restored colonial post office building
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant — Phnom Penh's most acclaimed fine-dining establishment offering French cuisine with Cambodian influences and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book your inter-city flight well in advance. Cambodia Angkor Air operates the Siem Reap–Phnom Penh route. Confirm luxury hotel booking in Phnom Penh separately. The Royal Palace is closed on public holidays and certain royal occasions — verify access.

day_by_day.morning: A deeply moving and important cultural experience: visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a detention and torture center during the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). A sobering but essential insight into Cambodia's recent history. Follow with a visit to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) with an audio guide — a memorial and museum dedicated to the victims.
day_by_day.afternoon: Decompress with a visit to the Psar Thmei (Central Market) — a stunning Art Deco landmark built in 1937 with a grand yellow dome. Browse stalls selling gold jewelry, silk, antiques, and local goods. Alternatively, visit the Russian Market (Psar Tuol Tom Poung) for artisan crafts and designer-label factory surplus. Visit the Wat Phnom hilltop temple — the spiritual heart of Phnom Penh.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on the Mekong River with Champagne and Cambodian canapés. Watch the city's skyline glow as the sun sets over the confluence of rivers. Return for a refined dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the luxury hotel — full buffet or à la carte with river views
meals.lunch: Lunch at Friends Restaurant (Romdeng) — a social enterprise restaurant training at-risk youth; exceptional Cambodian cuisine including deep-fried tarantulas for the adventurous
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Phnom Penh — sister restaurant to the Siem Reap original; beautifully presented Khmer dishes in a sophisticated garden villa

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. Photography is permitted but treat the sites with great respect. Consider hiring a survivor guide for a profoundly personal account.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer or short domestic flight from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 3.5–4 hours by road or 1 hour by air), then speedboat or private boat transfer to Koh Rong Samloem — one of Cambodia's most pristine and beautiful islands. Check in to a luxury eco-resort such as Song Saa Private Island or Koh Rong Samloem's premier beachfront villas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle in and spend the afternoon on Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay — some of the most beautiful beaches in Southeast Asia with powdery white sand and crystal-clear turquoise water. Enjoy snorkeling in the coral-rich waters, kayaking through mangroves, or simply relaxing in a private beach cabana with butler service.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent plankton experience — wade into the warm, dark sea at night to witness the magical blue glow of phosphorescent plankton lighting up the water around you. One of Cambodia's most magical natural spectacles. Return for a beachfront dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Phnom Penh hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at the island resort — grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and tropical salads with coconut water served beachside
meals.dinner: Romantic private beachfront dinner arranged by the resort — multi-course seafood tasting menu with torchlight, fresh flowers, and curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time for the islands — the seas are calming after the monsoon and visibility for snorkeling improves. Book island accommodation and boat transfers well in advance as premium options fill quickly. Bring cash as ATMs are limited on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise snorkeling or diving excursion to the coral reefs surrounding Koh Rong Samloem — the early morning offers the calmest seas and best visibility. Spot reef fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral formations. Non-divers can enjoy a glass-bottom boat tour. Return to resort for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot or by bicycle along jungle trails to hidden beaches and viewpoints. Visit the Marine Conservation Cambodia station to learn about reef restoration efforts and local marine biodiversity. Alternatively, indulge in a full afternoon of spa treatments at the resort — traditional Khmer massage, coconut oil body wraps, and aloe vera after-sun treatments.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour on the resort's private pier or beach deck. Watch the sky transform over the Gulf of Thailand. Casual yet refined dinner at the resort with fresh catch of the day.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast served on your private terrace or beachfront — tropical fruits, eggs to order, Cambodian rice porridge, fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch — grilled fish tacos, fresh spring rolls, coconut curry soup, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's main restaurant — wood-fired grilled seafood platter featuring the day's catch, accompanied by Cambodian herbs and premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Check with the resort about guided jungle treks and marine conservation activities. Tipping the dive guides and resort staff generously is customary and appreciated. Ensure sunscreen is reef-safe to protect the marine environment.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the island — enjoy a peaceful sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged by the resort, followed by a leisurely farewell breakfast. Take one last swim or kayak in the turquoise waters. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Speedboat transfer back to Sihanoukville and private vehicle transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport (or Sihanoukville Airport for direct connections). Allow ample travel time — approximately 4–5 hours total from island to Phnom Penh airport. Last-minute shopping at the airport for Cambodian coffee, silk scarves, and artisan chocolates.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Cambodia's ancient temples, vibrant culture, poignant history, and breathtaking islands.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the island resort — your choice of full spread with fresh tropical fruits, eggs benedict, Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a restaurant in Sihanoukville during the transit, or airport dining lounge
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or departure lounge meal depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all departure logistics — boat times, road transfers, and flight check-in — with your hotel concierge the evening before. Allow extra buffer time as island-to-airport transfers can be affected by sea conditions or traffic. Ensure all souvenirs comply with customs regulations — antiques and certain wildlife products cannot be exported from Cambodia.

query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026
